title: Release automation broken: public repo cannot call internal tech-scripts reusable workflows
description:
Both release caller workflows in this repo reference reusable workflows in axeptio/tech-scripts, which is an INTERNAL repository. This repo is PUBLIC.

GitHub rule: a public caller repository can only access reusable workflows from PUBLIC repositories.
https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/reusable-workflows

Evidence:
- gh workflow run create-release-pr.yml --ref develop -> 'workflow was not found. See .../reusing-workflows#access-to-reusable-workflows'
- auto-release.yml run 30255471346 (triggered by the PR #39 merge) failed with ZERO jobs = access-time failure
- axeptio/tech-scripts visibility=INTERNAL, actions access_level=organization
- This repo: allowed_actions=all, so it is NOT an allow-list problem
- The reusable workflow exists and is valid at pinned SHA 88cc1b36b18292319f78e840160909ac195a9306 with 'on: workflow_call'

Consequence: PR #38 (develop) and PR #39 (master) could never have worked. master now has auto-release.yml that fails on every push, and release-please was deleted, so this repo currently has NO working release automation and zero tags/releases.

Fix options:
(a) Revert to release-please authenticated with BOT_GITHUB_TOKEN - exactly the pattern used by the sibling PUBLIC repo axeptio-sgtm-public-template, proven working through v1.3.0. release-please-action is a public action so there is no access restriction.
(b) Mirror the tech-scripts reusable workflows into a PUBLIC repo.
(c) Inline the ~16KB reusable workflow body into this repo (creates drift from canonical, must be maintained).
(d) Make axeptio/tech-scripts public - not viable, internal tooling.

Recommended: (a).

Related: ENG-11756 (canonical release automation spec) assumes internal/private callers and does not cover public repos - the deploy-release-automation skill should gain a visibility precondition check.

comments.author: PLB
comments.text:
Fix is ready in PR #41 (base: develop) - all checks green (commitlint, CodeQL, Analyze). Blocked on merge: admin merge is required to bypass the 1-approval rule on develop, and that action is denied in this session.

Remaining after #41 merges:
1. Open and merge a develop -> master PR. This activates .github/workflows/release.yml and removes the dead auto-release.yml + gate file from master.
2. release-please then opens its first release PR. CHECK THE VERSION IT PICKS before merging - there is no prior tag, so it has no baseline; the manifest is seeded at 0.1.0.
3. Merging that release PR cuts the first tag + GitHub Release (repo currently has zero of both).

comments.author: PLB
comments.text:
Release automation is now correct on develop and master, but no release has been cut yet (still 0 tags).

Two defects found and fixed after the initial restore:
- PR #44: release-please-action's target-branch input is 'detected by default' and the detected value is the repo DEFAULT branch (develop), not the branch the workflow fires on. Without target-branch: master it released off develop.
- PR #46: that misconfigured run opened and merged PR #43 'chore(develop): release 0.1.1', creating a phantom release - VERSION/manifest/CHANGELOG bumped but no tag, no GitHub Release, and two compare links to tags that never existed. Reverted.

Still open: the first actual release, which will be v1.0.0 and is carried by PR #45 (license change, Release-As: 1.0.0).

title: Replace Apache 2.0 with Axeptio license notice (ENG-13012)
description:
Port of axeptio-sgtm-public-template commit e9ed1c6 (shipped as v1.2.0, 2026-07-22). Linear ENG-13012.

Apache 2.0 is irreversible for already-published gallery versions; it is replaced from version 1.0.0 onward. Notice cites 1.0.0, forced with a Release-As: 1.0.0 commit footer, since this repo has never cut a release.

Scope: LICENSE, README.md (License section), metadata.yaml (header only - versions: list untouched), new CONTRIBUTING.md. template.tpl is NOT touched (its ___TERMS_OF_SERVICE___ block is Google's mandatory gallery boilerplate).

Depends on the release automation landing (see gtm-22z / PR #41) for Release-As to take effect.

Also still pending under ENG-13012: axeptio-client-sgtm-public-template (public, still full Apache 2.0) - out of scope here.

title: Sync released version into metadata.yaml so the GTM Gallery publishes it
description:
The GTM Community Template Gallery publishes template versions from metadata.yaml's 'versions:' list (each entry is a commit sha + changeNotes). Nothing in the release flow updates that file, so a cut release does not reach the gallery - metadata.yaml stays hand-maintained.

Reference implementation: axeptio/axeptio-sgtm-public-template runs scripts/update-metadata-version.mjs after release-please publishes, then commits metadata.yaml with the bot's GPG key:

  - name: Sync metadata.yaml version history
    if: steps.release.outputs.release_created == 'true'
    env:
      RELEASE_TAG: ${{ steps.release.outputs.tag_name }}
      RELEASE_SHA: ${{ steps.release.outputs.sha }}
    run: node scripts/update-metadata-version.mjs

Port that script and wire it into whatever release mechanism this repo ends up with (see gtm-22z). If the canonical thin-caller auto-release.yml is used, the sync needs its own workflow keyed on 'release: published' since the caller cannot add steps.

changeNotes text still needs a human-meaningful summary - decide whether to derive it from the CHANGELOG entry or keep it hand-written.
